Eve_customer: Hi — exporting CSV from Console > Analytics > Usage for date range 2026-03-01 to 2026-03-10 just gives me the header row, no data. Happened twice today. Org: acme-corp, region: us-west1. Browser: Chrome 112 on macOS. File size is ~1.2KB. No console errors. Repro steps: 1) Console -> Analytics -> Usage 2) Set start/end dates (absolute) 3) Click 'Export CSV' 4) File downloads with only header. Attached screenshot and export id: exp_20260310_911.

Sam_support: Sorry about that, Eve — thanks for the clear repro. Can you confirm whether you used the timezone dropdown (Account TZ) or the "UTC" toggle in the date picker? Also can you paste the export id you mentioned (exp_20260310_911) and the exact CSV file you downloaded? If you can, a HAR for the download would help.

Eve_customer: I used the account timezone (America/Los_Angeles). Attached the CSV (header-only) and HAR. Export id is exp_20260310_911. Tried clearing cookies and incognito — same outcome.

Sam_support: Thanks — escalating to eng with logs and HAR. @Lucas_eng can you take a look? I included the HAR and the export id. Repro steps matched.

Lucas_eng: Looking now. I replayed the export with the same account TZ and export id. I can reproduce header-only when the end date is the current date and the account TZ != UTC.

Lucas_eng: Quick debugging notes: the analytics-export service builds a SQL WHERE on event_date with start_date <= event_date <= end_date, but the date parsing path casts the UI end_date string to a date at midnight UTC then converts to event_date (UTC) incorrectly, effectively making the end bound exclusive for non-UTC TZs. Off-by-one day when a user's TZ is behind UTC (e.g., PDT). Suspect change introduced in 2.3.0 when we switched to the new date parser.

Lucas_eng: Minimal repro script I used:

```
# repro via API
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/exports" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"org_id":"acme-corp","start_date":"2026-03-01","end_date":"2026-03-10","tz":"America/Los_Angeles","format":"csv"}'
```

Lucas_eng: Temporary workaround: set end_date to 2026-03-11 (one day forward) or switch the date picker to UTC. Also you can use the JSON export via the API which returns the raw rows.

Sam_support: Thanks, Lucas. Eve — for now please try the workaround (set end date to 2026-03-11) while we patch. Sorry for the inconvenience.

Eve_customer: Workaround worked, I got full rows when I used 3/11. Thanks.

Maya_devex: We've created a fix: date parser path will normalize UI dates using account TZ then apply inclusive end-of-day instead of midnight UTC. Patch PR #4821 targeting analytics-export service. Rolling a canary to staging now.

Lucas_eng: Post-deploy verification: re-ran the same export with exp_20260310_911 parameters and got full rows in CSV. Root cause: our date normalization used midnight UTC cast which excluded local-day events. Fixed to use end_of_day(account_tz) inclusive.

Sam_support: Eve — we've confirmed the fix and validated with your export id. Can you re-attempt the original export with the original end date (2026-03-10) and confirm you see rows now?

Eve_customer: Confirmed — exported with 3/10 and rows present. Thanks for the quick turnaround and for the clear workaround.

Sam_support: Closing the ticket. If you see anything else please reopen or DM me. :thumbsup:
notes: repro steps, export id exp_20260310_911, timezone-related off-by-one bug, fix rolled v2.3.1
